name: Document Request Chaser

nodes.name: Trigger Document Chaser At 8AM
nodes.notes: Fires every day at 8am (n8n server timezone). Feeds 'Fetch Firm Users From Clio' first, which passes straight through into 'Fetch Outstanding Document Tasks From Clio' — a genuine sequential dependency, not a disconnected side-fetch (see that node's notes for why this matters, confirmed live while building PAC-64). Every pending task is re-checked on every run — there's no separate list of 'already reminded' to maintain, because each task's own due date tells this workflow exactly which tier (if any) applies today.

nodes.name: Fetch Firm Users From Clio API
nodes.notes:
Fetches the firm's user directory once per run — used by 'Build Document Reminder Email' and 'Build Staff Escalation Email' to resolve a task's assignee id to a real name and email, so reminders can mention the responsible staff member and the urgent-tier escalation reaches the right person. Requesting 'email' works here because /users.json is the primary resource, not a nested association (Clio rejects a nested User's email — confirmed live in PAC-63).

This node's output is passed straight through into 'Fetch Outstanding Document Tasks From Clio' unchanged (that node makes its own independent API call) — wiring it in series like this, rather than as a disconnected side-fetch referenced only by name, is what makes n8n reliably execute it on every run and every testing method. A node with an incoming connection but no outgoing one is not guaranteed to run (confirmed the hard way in PAC-64).

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58/59/61/63/64 — reuse it if already deployed.

nodes.name: Fetch Open Matters From Clio API
nodes.notes:
Fetches every open matter once per run — used by 'Compute Days Overdue And Escalation Tier' to resolve a task's matter id to the client's real name and email.

Clio rejects a doubly-nested field request: tasks.json's 'matter{...,client{...}}' fails with 'InvalidFields: matter} is not a valid field' (confirmed live) — Clio's field selector apparently only supports one level of nesting, and client{...} nested inside matter{...} nested inside the tasks fetch is two levels deep. 'client{id,name,primary_email_address}' nested just one level under matters.json, by contrast, is exactly the pattern PAC-64 already confirmed works live. So instead of trying to get the client in one call, this fetches matters separately and 'Compute Days Overdue And Escalation Tier' resolves each task's matter id against it — the same lookup-table approach already used for the assignee/user directory.

Same Clio OAuth2 credential as the other two fetches — no separate setup.

nodes.name: Fetch Outstanding Document Tasks
nodes.notes:
Pulls every task still marked 'pending' in Clio, regardless of type — the next few nodes filter down to just document requests. Same tasks.json request pattern as PAC-59/61/63, with 'pending' as the status value.

A document request is tracked as a Clio task: name it what's needed (e.g. 'Photo ID from client'), set a due date, assign it to whoever is chasing it, and use a dedicated task type (default 'Document Request', configurable via FIRM_DOCUMENT_REQUEST_TASK_TYPE) so this workflow can tell it apart from ordinary to-dos. Marking the task complete once the document arrives is what stops future reminders — there's no separate 'stop reminding' step anywhere in this workflow.

Only one level of nested fields is requested here ('task_type{id,name}', 'assignee{id,name}', 'matter{id,display_number,description}', with no client nested inside matter) — see 'Fetch Open Matters From Clio' for why a doubly-nested client request is rejected. 'task_type' and 'assignee' as nested fields follow the same conventions this catalog already uses (NTC-17, PAC-59) but haven't themselves been independently confirmed live — check your first real run's output and adjust if Clio rejects either.

'Never Error' is on, and downstream filtering treats a missing/empty 'data' array the same as zero tasks.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as the other two fetches above — no separate setup.

nodes.name: Split Out Document Task Records
nodes.notes: Turns the single API response into one n8n item per task, so the Filter and Code nodes downstream can each operate on individual tasks. An empty or missing 'data' array (e.g. after a Clio error) simply produces zero items.

nodes.name: Filter Tasks With Valid Due Date
nodes.notes: Drops anything that isn't a Document Request task (ordinary to-dos, deadlines, etc.), or one with no due date. The client-email check happens later, after 'Compute Days Overdue And Escalation Tier' resolves it from the separate matters lookup — a task's own matter object doesn't carry the client here (see that fetch's notes for why).

nodes.name: Calculate Overdue Days And Tier
nodes.notes: Runs once per task (mode: Run Once for Each Item). Every task gets a 'tier' field — empty string if today isn't one of its three escalation windows — which the next node filters on, alongside whether the client email actually resolved. A task that isn't yet overdue at all (daysOverdue <= 0) simply gets tier: '' like any other non-matching day.

nodes.name: Filter Tasks Due For Reminder
nodes.notes: Drops any task whose days-overdue didn't land on exactly one of the three tier windows, and any task whose matter didn't resolve to a client with an email on file (unassigned client, matter not in the open-matters fetch, etc.) — there's nobody to send the reminder to. Only tasks actually due for a reminder, with somewhere to send it, survive to the next step.

nodes.name: Check For Any Reminders Today
nodes.notes: Run Once for All Items (the default) — needs to see whether anything survived the filters above, not one task at a time.

nodes.name: If Reminder Is Due Today
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one document request hit a tier today) → build and send the client reminder, and separately check whether it also needs a staff escalation.
No (nothing due — most days, for most firms) → route to Skip. No email sent.

nodes.name: Skip No Documents To Chase
nodes.notes: No outstanding document request hit one of the three escalation tiers today. Expected on most days — this is normal, not a failure.

nodes.name: Build Document Reminder Email Body
nodes.notes:
Do not add an opt-out footer to 'message' (the plain-text body) — the compliance guardrail (next node) appends it automatically to that version and logs the send attempt. 'email_html' carries its own independently-built matching footer, since the guardrail never sees or touches the HTML version.

FIRM_CLIENT_PORTAL_URL is optional — copy adapts gracefully if unset. Personalization (assignee's contact email) degrades gracefully to the generic firm address if the assignee can't be resolved.

nodes.name: Execute Compliance Workflow
nodes.notes:
Checks whether this client has opted out of firm emails. If not, appends the required unsubscribe footer and logs the send attempt to the audit sheet — same client-facing pattern as PAC-18 and PAC-64.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable.

Returns: { approved, message_out, recipient, suppression_reason } plus all upstream fields.

nodes.name: If Reminder Is Approved
nodes.notes:
Yes (client hasn't opted out) → send.
No (client has opted out of firm emails) → route to Skip. The suppression is already logged by the guardrail.

nodes.name: Send Document Reminder Email
nodes.notes:
Sends the compliance-approved reminder to the client — both the plain-text body (from 'text', using message_out from the guardrail, which carries the required unsubscribe footer) and the styled HTML body. The HTML field must reach back to '$('Build Document Reminder Email').item.json.email_html' rather than plain '$json.email_html' — the guardrail call immediately upstream replaces $json with its own response, which doesn't carry email_html (confirmed live: this was wired as plain $json initially and silently sent a blank email — visible only as 'undefined' under the HTML field's expression preview, not as an error anywhere).

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: Skip Client Opt-Out Reminder
nodes.notes: This client has opted out of firm emails. The suppression is already logged by the guardrail workflow. No email is sent.

nodes.name: If Reminder Tier Is Urgent
nodes.notes:
Yes (14-15 days overdue) → also alert the responsible staff member directly, on top of the client reminder built in the row above.
No (reminder or second_reminder tier) → no staff escalation yet, route to Skip.

nodes.name: Skip No Staff Escalation Needed
nodes.notes: This document request isn't at the urgent tier yet — no internal escalation needed. The client still gets their own reminder from the row above.

nodes.name: Build Staff Escalation Email Body
nodes.notes: FIRM_PARALEGAL_EMAIL is optional — falls back to FIRM_EMAIL if unset. If neither the assignee resolves nor either variable is set, this throws rather than silently escalating to nobody.

nodes.name: Send Staff Escalation Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the internal escalation to the responsible staff member (or the fallback address). Same SMTP credential as the client reminder — no separate setup.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

parameters.content:
## Document Request Chaser

### How it works

1. Triggers daily, fetches the firm's user directory (used to personalize with the assigned staff member's name), then every open matter, then every pending Clio task — each in sequence, so every lookup is a real dependency n8n always resolves correctly. Matters are fetched separately because Clio rejects a doubly-nested client{...} request on tasks.json.
2. Splits tasks into individual records, keeps only ones that are actually document requests (a configurable Clio task type) with a due date on file, then computes each one's days-overdue, resolves the client's email from the matters lookup, and matches the tier.
3. A second filter keeps only tasks hitting a tier today, with a client email that actually resolved — 1-2 days overdue (reminder), 7-8 days (second reminder), 14-15 days (urgent) — all with native n8n nodes.
4. The matching reminder is built (styled HTML + plain text), checked against the compliance guardrail (opt-out + disclaimer), then sent to the client if approved.
5. At the urgent tier, a separate internal email also alerts the responsible staff member (resolved by name via the user directory) that the request may need a phone call — bypassing the guardrail since it's an internal message, not a client one.
6. Skips silently, with a clearly labelled entry in execution history, on a day with nothing due. Marking the Clio task complete once the document arrives stops all future reminders automatically — there's nothing else to update.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Set up the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) first — every client-facing reminder here goes through it.
- [ ] Configure Clio OAuth2 credentials with task, matter, and user-directory read access.
- [ ] Configure SMTP credentials for sending.
- [ ] Create (or confirm) a Clio task type named 'Document Request' — every outstanding document should be tracked as one task of this type, due-dated, assigned to whoever is chasing it, and linked to its matter.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: CLIO_BASE_URL, FIRM_NAME, FIRM_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID.
- [ ] Optionally set FIRM_CLIENT_PORTAL_URL, FIRM_DOCUMENT_REQUEST_TASK_TYPE, FIRM_PARALEGAL_EMAIL.

### Customization

Edit the three tiers' subject/body copy in 'Build Document Reminder Email Body' — one node handles all three, same pattern as the Invoice Reminder Ladder (PAC-18). Change the escalation timing by editing the day windows in 'Calculate Overdue Days And Tier'.

## Resolve who to personalize with, then fetch document requests

Fetches the firm's user directory, then every open matter, then every pending task — each passed straight through into the next in sequence, making every fetch a genuine upstream step (not a disconnected side-fetch) so n8n always resolves them, on every run and every testing method. Matters are fetched separately from tasks because Clio rejects a doubly-nested client{...} request on tasks.json.

## Split, filter, and tier

Keeps only pending tasks that are document requests with a due date, computes each one's days-overdue, resolves the client's email from the matters lookup, then keeps only the ones hitting an escalation tier today — all native n8n nodes.

## Check for anything due today

Bridges the native filter chain back to a clean, labelled Skip if nothing survived — matches the explicit-skip pattern used across this catalog.

## Send the client reminder

Builds the tiered reminder (styled HTML + plain text), routes it through the compliance guardrail for opt-out checking and the required disclaimer, then sends it if approved.

## Escalate to staff if urgent

At the 14-15 day tier, also alerts the responsible staff member directly — an internal email, so it bypasses the client-facing guardrail entirely, same as PAC-18's partner escalation.

main.node: Fetch Firm Users From Clio API
Fetch Open Matters From Clio API
Filter Tasks With Valid Due Date

description: Fires daily, fetches the firm's user directory from Clio, then every open matter, then every pending task. Filters down to document-request tasks (a configurable Clio task type) with a due date, resolves each one's client email from the matters lookup, computes days-overdue, and matches it against three escalation tiers: 1-2 days overdue (reminder), 7-8 days (second reminder), 14-15 days (urgent). The matching reminder is personalized with the responsible staff member's contact details where resolvable, checked against the Bar-Compliance Guardrail for opt-out and disclaimer, then sent if approved. At the urgent tier, a separate internal email also alerts the staff member directly, bypassing the guardrail since it's not a client message. Marking the Clio task complete stops all future reminders automatically. Replaces the manual paralegal follow-up that eats time chasing outstanding client documents.
